name: Meremoth
title: The Priest Who Rebuilt the Walls
summary: Meremoth, son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, was a priest who played an important role in rebuilding Jerusalem after the exile. He was involved in weighing the temple treasures brought back from Babylon and actively participated in rebuilding Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah. He is also mentioned among those who sealed the covenant with God.

keyEvents.title: Weighing the Temple Treasures
keyEvents.description: Meremoth, son of Uriah the priest, was responsible for weighing the silver, gold, and vessels that Ezra and the returning exiles brought from Babylon to the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the Wall – First Section
keyEvents.description: Meremoth, son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, rebuilt a section of Jerusalem's wall next to Eliashib under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the Wall – Second Section
keyEvents.description: Meremoth also rebuilt another part of the wall, from the entrance of the high priest Eliashib's house to its end.

keyEvents.title: Sealing the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Meremoth was among the priests who sealed the solemn covenant to follow God's law, as it was read aloud by Ezra and confirmed under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Genealogy of the Priests
keyEvents.description: The lineage of Meremoth, descendants of Hakkoz, is mentioned in connection with the registration of priests returning from exile, and they initially had difficulty proving their ancestry.
